description: fz has no Macro module. Elixir's Macro.escape/1 (:elixir_quote.escape): atoms, numbers, binaries, 2-tuples and lists are their own code (elements escaped); other tuples become {:{}, [], elems}; maps (and structs) become {:%{}, [], pairs}; a ref, a PID or a function is refused. In fz a PID is refused too (a compile-time PID means nothing in a built program; user decision on fz-sc8.144), and so is a remote capture until its own ticket lands, with a message naming the gap. Done when: lib Macro.escape matches Elixir's output for each kind (oracle fixture, including a macro that unquotes an escaped map), and refusals are fixtures.
title: Macro.escape/1 turns a value into the quoted code that rebuilds it
